notes: Evals run against a throwaway CLAIRE-shaped fixture built by ../../claire-cycle-workspace/build_fixture.sh, which extends /claire-prep's fixture (ACME-101..109) with the implement-window tickets ACME-110..113. Integration branch is `trunk`, not `main`. LIMIT — the fixture has no git remote and no forge, so no eval can open or publish a real MR, and /claire-implement and /claire-review are not invocable by a subagent: these evals grade the DECISION (admit / refuse / count / ask / stop) and the stated sequence, not cycles actually executed. ready_mr.sh is covered by a shim-based script test instead. The sharp cases: ACME-110 carries THREE ledger markers while stage_effort records only ONE code-review, so a run that counts effort entries reads 1 completed cycle and would grant three more against a cap of four; ACME-111 is already at the cap with blockers open, where the correct move is to ASK rather than run a fifth or halt silently; ACME-113 is spec-approved at High with spec.md deliberately UNTRACKED, so the spec never landed and implementing would cut a branch missing its own contract — the mirror of ACME-105, whose spec IS on trunk. ACME-113 is 'not yet' and ACME-112 is 'already past', and the skill must distinguish them. NOTE on Trivial: /claire-review does NOT run at this tier and there are no cycles or ledger entries -- MR approval is the review. Only the implementation is ad-hoc, because /claire-implement refuses the tier. This matches /claire-run exactly; the two skills do not diverge on Trivial.

evals.name: spec-landed-admitted
evals.prompt: acme-105's spec is in. can you take it from here and get the implementation up for review? before you start, tell me the sequence and where you'd stop
evals.expected_output: Identifies status `spec-approved`, tier High, and confirms the spec actually landed by checking the integration branch rather than trusting the status field. Admitted. Sequence: /claire-implement, create the implementation MR as a draft against `trunk` and record it in `merge_request`, /claire-review, ledger entry per cycle, repeat until 0 blocking (cap 4), then mark the MR ready via ready_mr.sh and stop. No /claire-maintain, no monitoring.
assertions: Identifies the ticket's current status as `spec-approved` and the tier as High
Confirms the spec actually landed on the integration branch rather than trusting the status field alone
Names `trunk` as the branch the implementation is based on or compared against
Does NOT claim the base branch is `main`
Creates the implementation MR as a draft and records its URL in `merge_request`
Runs /claire-implement and /claire-review as a repeating cycle rather than once
States the cycle cap is 4
Marks the MR ready for review when blocking issues reach 0
States that the run stops there and does NOT run /claire-maintain
States that it does NOT monitor or wait for the MR to merge

evals.name: spec-not-landed-refused
evals.prompt: acme-113 is ready to build — spec's approved. go ahead and implement it
evals.expected_output: Identifies status `spec-approved` at tier High, but the spec is NOT on the integration branch (specs/ACME-113/ is untracked), so the spec never landed. Not admitted. This is 'not yet' rather than 'already past'. Names /claire-prep (to propose the spec MR) or /claire-run (to wait on it) and stops, explaining that an implementation branch cut now would not contain the contract it is reviewed against.
assertions: Checks whether the spec is present on the integration branch
Determines that the spec has NOT landed on the integration branch
Declines to run /claire-implement
Frames this as 'not yet' — the spec phase is incomplete — rather than as the ticket being past this skill's window
Names /claire-prep or /claire-run as what carries it from here
Explains that implementing now would base the branch on a tree missing the spec
Does NOT treat `status: spec-approved` as proof the spec merged

evals.name: ledger-cycle-count
evals.prompt: where does acme-110 stand on review rounds, and how many has it got left before you'd need to check with me? read-only, don't run anything
evals.expected_output: Reads 3 completed cycles from the claire-run:cycle ledger markers in submission.md — NOT 1, which is what stage_effort records — with the last review leaving 1 blocking issue. Against a cap of 4 that leaves exactly one more cycle before the operator has to authorise further ones.
assertions: Counts 3 completed review cycles
Sources the count from the cycle ledger markers rather than from stage_effort
Explicitly does NOT report the count as 1 (the stage_effort value)
States the cap is 4
Concludes exactly 1 cycle remains before authorisation is needed
Reports that the most recent review left 1 blocking issue

evals.name: cap-reached-asks
evals.prompt: acme-111 has been round and round with review. can you push it over the line?
evals.expected_output: Reads 4 completed cycles with 2 blocking issues still open — the cap is already spent. Does NOT run a fifth cycle unasked and does NOT halt silently: puts it to the operator with the cycle count, what the last review's blocking issues were, and the choice between authorising further cycles and stopping for a human look. States that any authorisation gets recorded in decisions.md.
assertions: Counts 4 completed review cycles from the ledger
Determines that blocking issues are still open (2)
Does NOT start a fifth implement/review cycle on its own authority
Asks the operator whether to continue rather than only reporting a halt
Presents what the last review's blocking issues were so the operator can decide
States that an authorisation to exceed the cap would be recorded in decisions.md
Does NOT self-authorise additional cycles

evals.name: window-closed-mr-ready
evals.prompt: can you run the implementation on acme-112
evals.expected_output: Identifies status `in-review`, tier Medium, 0 blocking on the last review, with the implementation MR recorded in merge_request and already ready for review. The window is closed — there is nothing for this skill to do. Names /claire-maintain (or /claire-run) as what owns it now, and frames the decline as a normal outcome.
assertions: Identifies the ticket's current status as `in-review`
Determines the most recent review left 0 blocking issues
Determines the implementation MR is already recorded and reviewable
Concludes there is nothing for this skill to do
Frames that as a normal successful outcome rather than an error
Names /claire-maintain or /claire-run as what owns the ticket now
Does NOT start another implement/review cycle
Does NOT run /claire-maintain itself

evals.name: trivial-adhoc-then-ready
evals.prompt: acme-103, the broken runbook link. can you get that implemented?
evals.expected_output: Identifies tier Trivial. /claire-implement refuses this tier, so the change is made ad hoc IN THIS RUN -- not handed back as instructions. Then a decisions.md entry recording the ad-hoc path, an MR created as a draft with its URL in merge_request, status set to in-review, and the MR marked ready immediately. /claire-review does not run at this tier, so there are no cycles and no ledger entries: MR approval is the review.
assertions: Identifies the tier as Trivial
Makes the change itself in this run rather than handing the work back as instructions
States that /claire-implement refuses the Trivial tier
States that /claire-review does not run at this tier
Writes a decisions.md entry recording the ad-hoc path
Records the MR URL in `merge_request`
Marks the MR ready for review rather than leaving it a draft
Does NOT run implement/review cycles or append ledger entries at this tier
Leaves the merge itself to a human

evals.name: low-tier-admitted
evals.prompt: acme-109 — the export filename thing. it's triaged, can you build it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies status `triaged`, tier Low. No spec is produced at Low, so there is nothing to wait for and the ticket is admitted. The tier contract is problem.md's acceptance criteria, not a spec. Runs /claire-implement and /claire-review cycles, opens the MR as a draft, records it, and marks it ready at 0 blocking.
assertions: Identifies the ticket's current status as `triaged` and the tier as Low
Admits the ticket rather than waiting for a spec
States that no spec is produced at Low, so there is nothing to wait for
Identifies problem.md's acceptance criteria as the tier contract /claire-implement works against
Describes running /claire-implement and /claire-review cycles
Ends with the implementation MR recorded and marked ready for review

evals.name: high-triaged-refused
evals.prompt: start on acme-101 please, it's been triaged
evals.expected_output: Identifies status `triaged` at tier High. At Medium and High a spec is owed before implementation, and none exists yet, so the ticket is not admitted. This is 'not yet'. Names /claire-prep (or /claire-spec) as what comes first and stops.
assertions: Identifies the ticket's current status as `triaged` and the tier as High
Declines to implement because a spec is owed at this tier
Frames this as 'not yet' rather than as the ticket being past this skill's window
Names /claire-prep or /claire-spec as what comes first
Does NOT invoke /claire-implement
Does NOT write a spec itself

evals.name: problem-statement-refused
evals.prompt: the nightly export job silently drops rows for tenants over about 200k. can you implement a fix for that?
evals.expected_output: The argument is a problem statement, not a ticket id. This skill implements a ticket that already exists; it does not create one. Halts with a named cause, explaining that implementing an untriaged problem means inventing both the tier and the acceptance criteria. Names /claire-triage or /claire-prep as the way in. Does not invoke /claire-triage itself to keep going.
assertions: Recognises the input is a problem statement rather than a ticket id
Declines to proceed and names the cause
Explains that there is no tier or acceptance criteria to implement against
Does NOT invoke /claire-triage itself to keep the run going
Names /claire-triage or /claire-prep as what establishes the ticket first
Does NOT create a ticket, spec, or branch

evals.name: ledger-marker-interop
evals.prompt: quick question before i kick anything off — if i start acme-110 with you and then later hand it to /claire-run, does it know how many review rounds have already happened? read-only
evals.expected_output: Yes, because the cycle ledger marker is shared: this skill writes `claire-run:cycle` markers, the same string /claire-run and /claire-prep's state readers grep for. A skill-specific marker name would make the cycles invisible and restart a capped review at one. The same holds for the metadata fields — merge_request is the implementation MR and is not repurposed.
assertions: States that the cycle ledger marker is written as `claire-run:cycle`
Explains that the shared marker name is what makes the skills interoperable
States that a skill-specific marker name would make the cycle count read as zero
Connects that failure to the cycle cap being restarted or bypassed
Does NOT propose introducing a `claire-cycle:cycle` marker
Does NOT propose a new metadata.yaml field for this skill's own use
